data.name: Help_1_B
data.value: The tool waits for the radio to start. Switch the radio off, leave the cable in, press **Try again**, and when the yellow **"Switch the radio off and on now"** shows, switch the radio off if it is on, then on. If it comes up with the normal screen, switch it off and on once more. Do not press any keys.

data.name: Help_2_B
data.value: Plug the programming cable firmly into the computer and the radio, press **Refresh**. The DM-32UV cable usually shows as "USB-SERIAL CH340" (the program picks it by itself). If it does not show, install the CH340 driver. Virtual ports (com0com, Bluetooth) are not the radio and are never picked.

data.name: Help_3_B
data.value: An install needs the radio's **current** backup. If the radio changed after that backup (another install, writing with the CPS) the installer notices and stops without writing anything. Make a new backup.

data.name: Help_4_B
data.value: The program installs only **signed** DDM32 Plus versions: the version list's signature must verify with the key in the program and the downloaded file's SHA-256 must equal the listed one. Versions whose signature fails are not listed (Details on the "Versions" page).

data.name: Help_5_B
data.value: If the radio runs stock firmware the program sees it in the backup and prepares the radio's own DMR codec from your backup in the reserved codec area. DDM32 Plus was tried only on stock .047; other supported stock versions (.032 - .049) show a warning. For unknown versions (for example .050) first install Open25-DM32 Classic with its own Flasher, then DDM32 Plus over it.

data.name: Help_6_B
data.value: The program never tries again by itself. If it says "Nothing was written" the radio was not switched on in time: you may do the Check and Install steps again. If it says "Stopped after writing started" do not switch the radio off, do not unplug the cable, and restore the backup taken before the install on the **Go back** page. The bootloader is never written, so the radio stays installable.

data.name: Help_7_B
data.value: In the **backups** folder inside the program folder: {0} **Do not delete it and do not share it**: it holds your radio's calibration and channels. Program updates and uninstalling never touch it. The previous program's backups stay in its own folder (%LOCALAPPDATA%\DDM32Plus or DDM25Plus).

data.name: Help_8_B
data.value: If, with the cable plugged in, Device Manager does not show "USB-SERIAL CH340" under "Ports (COM & LPT)", the driver is missing. Download the driver from the cable maker or from WCH's site (CH341SER), install it, then unplug and replug the cable.

data.name: Pack_Text
data.value: Data packs are lists the radio keeps on its data chip: the **RadioID pack** (callers' names for DMR IDs) and the **air band pack** (each airfield's frequencies). This page builds them on your PC from files **you download yourself** (radioid.net, your State's AIP pages) and writes one to the radio. Nothing of these lists comes with the program. Optional: the radio works without packs. Needs DDM32 Plus v1.0.0-beta.4 or newer on the radio.

data.name: Pack_OnRadioText
data.value: The radio must be switched on and running DDM32 Plus, with the cable in; it does not need to be switched off and on. The live read uses the radio's own programming (CPS) protocol and only reads. A verified backup shows what the radio held when it was made (files only).

Then choose the countries (comma separated, as RadioID.net writes them) and build the pack. The list stays on your PC; the program never passes it on.

An airfield the pack names gets the pack's frequency list on the radio; the others keep the built-in table.

data.name: Pack_WriteText
data.value: The pack goes into the slot **not in force**: its sectors first, its header last. Until the last sector the radio keeps the pack it has; if anything goes wrong, that pack stays. Only the data pack region of the data chip (0xE70000-0xEFFFFF) is written; the program refuses every other address. The radio stays switched on.
